promises.text: The Border road was laid on a Dunmer line from Stormhold to Thorn. West of the Greenspring track it drops off the ridge into the river marsh.

confirmed.note: The road comes down off the ridge west of the Greenspring track and crosses the river marsh on the river plank run.

promises.text: Nobody lives on the crossings. Greenspring keeps the planks because its trade goes out along this road.

confirmed.note: No dwelling or bed on the crossings; the layout holds plank runs, rocks, cairns, a cold fire ring and a grave only.

promises.text: The marsh rots the piles in a few seasons. Greenspring has to keep replacing them.

confirmed.note: Both runs stand on piles in standing marsh water (17 dock pieces, wet ground under each run).

promises.text: The road keeps to the dry strip at the mountain foot and crosses water only where it must: two reaches of the river marsh, where the water stands up to a metre and a quarter deep.

confirmed.note: Two plank runs: the river run, 9 pieces at about (4475, 1560-1626) over crossing.major.009, and the inlet run, 8 pieces at about (4659-4713, 1787-1812) over crossing.major.012; the ground under them lies 0.05 to 1.22 m below the water surface, and the road between them keeps to the bank at 1.4 to 8 m.

promises.text: A stone causeway would replace the planks if anyone paid for one.

confirmed.note: Both crossings are timber plank runs; no stone causeway is placed.

promises.text: the Border road crossings below Greenspring shows the plank crossing its record names.
